evidence.quote: Most Dwarf words have several meanings.
evidence.claim: Selected senses are explicit; neutral concatenated sign names are Forthammer compositions, not attested hospital names or a complete official naming grammar.

evidence.quote: medical care and reassurance to wounded or ailing Dwarfs
evidence.claim: Dwarf medical care is attested. This religious career context is not evidence that any generated DF hospital is a temple or staffed by priests. No dedication, ritual, skill or cure is assigned.

evidence.section: Dwarf early history / War Against Chaos
evidence.claim: This is a particular ancestral and magical context, not a secular hospital-naming convention. It supports excluding unverified divine dedication and magical protection from these names; it supplies no vocabulary in this pack.

The inscription context grounds material depictions of existing neutral eye and sun emblems. These are adapted sign images, not source-attested medical symbols, magical runes, actual furnishings or treatments.

Peacetime craftsmanship supplies context for stone carving and architectural emblems. It establishes no hospital naming custom and does not certify the actual location's architecture, quality or safety.
Silver and bread are attested independent concepts, not invented product or wealth claims.
The selected moonlight sense and the printed material, shadow, work and sunrise nouns add distinct concepts. No generic machine, dawn-direction, geology or ancestry meaning is invented.

The conjunction explicitly pairs two reviewed images. Thrag means wound, Thrynaz includes laws, Tiwaz includes rest and Skaud includes song. These are not new translations for hospital, government or tavern.

evidence.quote: Dwarf medical theory looks upon the body as a machine
evidence.claim: Physicians, surgeons and infirmaries are attested. Anatomy, observation, records and rest are cautious adapted care imagery, not official medical insignia or an assertion of a treatment outcome.
